# Cadence

> Cadence is an ambient context layer for Claude Code. It reads the room — the intent in your prompt, music, time of day, self-reported state, git activity — and injects that state into every prompt so the agent can respond like someone who actually knows what you're in the middle of.

Cadence is built by Cullum & Co (https://cullum.co). It is an open-source (MIT) Claude Code plugin, built for the Mac (alpha), distributed via npm as `@cullumco/cadence`. The GitHub README is the canonical, complete documentation; this site is the why.

## What it does

- Gathers ambient signals: prompt intent (ship/think/debug read from your own words), currently playing music, time of day, git work-state, prompt rhythm, and self-reported state (`/cadence:state`).
- Privacy-adjacent signals (typing tempo, focused app, Spotify link, horoscope/moon) are opt-in and off by default; `cadence pause` silences everything instantly.
- Infers four cadence dials — pace, tone, posture, proactivity — and injects them into every prompt as advisory context.
- Gives the agent a reframe lens: read the prompt the way someone in that state meant it, without overriding the user's literal words.
- Conservative Stop and PostToolUse hooks: catches soft handoffs when you're shipping, and speaks once when the repo enters/leaves a conflict or a destructive-git streak.

## Who it's for

Developer-practitioners who use Claude Code seriously — engineers, writers, and makers who are in their tools all day and notice when something is thoughtful versus generic.

## Install

- `/plugin marketplace add cullumco/cadence`
- `/plugin install cadence@cadence`
- `/cadence:setup` — conversational setup; `/cadence:pause` — instant off switch
